<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{cycles_and_fixed_points_scalar}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a protograph-based code with parity-check matrix $H={\left[\begin{matrix}H_{ij}\end{matrix}\right]}_{n_c\times n_v}$. Let $W$ be a TBC walk of length $2l$ in the protograph $G_B$ having edge sequence $e_1, e_2,\dots,e_{2l}$ with associated permutation matrices $P_1, P_2,\dots,P_{2l}$. Then the Tanner graph has a $2l$-cycle if the product $P_1P_2^\top P_3P_4^\top\cdots P_{2l-1}P_{2l}^\top$ has a fixed point.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cycles_and_fixed_points_pp}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a protograph-based code with parity-check matrix $H={\left[\begin{matrix}H_{ij}\end{matrix}\right]}_{n_c\times n_v}$. Let $W$ be a TBC walk of length $2l$ in the protograph $G_B$ having edge sequence $e_1, e_2,\dots,e_{2l}$ with associated permutation matrices $P_1, P_2,\dots,P_{2l}$. If the corresponding permutation polynomials are $p_1, p_2,\dots,p_{2l}$, then the Tanner graph has a $2l$-cycle if the composition $p_{2l}^{-1} \circ p_{2l-1} \circ \cdots \circ p_4^{-1} \circ p_3 \circ p_2^{-1} \circ p_1$ has a fixed point.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{girth_upper_bound_12_powers_of_x}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a protograph-based code with parity-check matrix $H$ with monomials. 
If $n_c\geq2$ and $n_v\geq3$, then $\text{girth}(H)\leq12$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Consider any $2\times3$ submatrix $[x^a, x^b, x^c; x^d, x^e, x^f]$
of $H$ and let $W=[e_a, \allowbreak e_d,\allowbreak e_f, \allowbreak e_c, \allowbreak e_b, \allowbreak e_e, \allowbreak e_d, \allowbreak e_a, \allowbreak e_c, \allowbreak e_f, \allowbreak e_e, \allowbreak e_b]$, where $e_k$ is the edge associated to $x^k$. Then $W$ is a TBC walk in the protograph with 
$x^{a d^{-1} f c^{-1} b e^{-1} d a^{-1} c f^{-1} e b^{-1}}=x.$
Since $x$ has fixed points, 12-cycles are unavoidable.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{minimum_distance_upper_bound_powers_of_x}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a protograph-based code with parity-check matrix $H$ with monomials. 
Then the minimum distance of $\mathcal{C}$ is upper bounded by $(n_c+1)!$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
The permutation matrices obtained from permutation polynomials of the form $f(x)=x^n$ are commutative, so Theorem 2 in \cite{md01} applies.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{composition_of_binomials}
Let $q$ be odd and consider the polynomials $f_1(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx,f_2(x)=cx^{(q+1)/2}+dx\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$. Then the composition $(f_2\circ f_1)(x)$ is given by
\begin{equation*}
(ce+da)x^{(q+1)/2}+(cf+db)x\mod(x^q-x)
,\end{equation*}
where $e+f={(a+b)}^{(q+1)/2}$ and $e+f={(b-a)}^{(q+1)/2}$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{binomials_permutation_polynomials}
The polynomial $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$ is a permutation polynomial of $\mathbb{F}_q$ if and only if $b^2-a^2 \in S$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
The permutation polynomial $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$ is piecewise affine.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Consider the quadratic character $\psi : \mathbb{F}_q \rightarrow \{0,1,-1\}$ defined by $\psi(x)=x^{(q-1)/2}$. Then
\vspace{-2mm}
\begin{equation*}
\psi(x) = 
\begin{cases} 
0, & \text{if } x=0, \\
1, & \text{if } x \in S, \\
-1, & \text{if } x \in N.
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
We can rewrite the polynomial $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$ as
\begin{align*}
f(x) &= ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx = (ax^{(q-1)/2}+b)x =(a\psi(x)+b)x,
\end{align*}
and by substituting the values for $\psi(x)$, we get
\begin{equation}
\label{pw-fn}
f(x) = 
\begin{cases} 
0, & \text{if } x=0, \\
f_{+}(x):=(b+a)x, & \text{if } x \in S, \\
f_{-}(x):=(b-a)x, & \text{if } x \in N.
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
The permutation polynomial $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$ has $x=0$ as its only fixed point if and only if $b\pm a\neq 1$.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
This is clear from \eqref{pw-fn}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{theorem_condition_only_0_fixed_point}
The composition $F=f_n\circ\cdots\circ f_2\circ f_1$ with permutation polynomials $f_i(x)=a_ix^{(q+1)/2}+b_ix$ has $x=0$ as its only fixed point if and only if $M_S,M_N,M_S',M_N'\neq 1$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{definition_type_square_nonsquare}
For $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$ with $b^2-a^2\in S$, we say that $f$ (and its corresponding permutation matrix) is of type $\bm{\mathsf{S}}$ if $b\pm a\in S$, and of type $\bm{\mathsf{N}}$ if $b\pm a\in N$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{girth_upper_bound_binomials}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a protograph-based code with parity-check matrix $H$ using $f(x)=ax^{(q+1)/2}+bx$. 
Then we have the following.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item If the protograph has a $2\times3$ all-ones submatrix, then $\text{girth}(H)\leq20$.
    \item If the protograph has a $2\times4$ all-ones submatrix, then $\text{girth}(H)\leq16$.
    \item If the protograph has a $2\times L$ all-ones submatrix with $L\geq5$, then $\text{girth}(H)\leq12$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
For $L\geq3$, consider any $2\times L$ submatrix
\begin{equation*}
B_{2\times L}=\left[\begin{matrix}f_1&f_2&f_3&\cdots&f_L \\ f_{L+1}&f_{L+2}&f_{L+3}&\cdots&f_{2L}\end{matrix}\right]
\end{equation*}
of $H$, 
where $f_i=a_ix^{(q+1)/2}+b_ix$ satisfies $b_i^2-a_i^2\in S$ for each $i$.

(a) Take all the columns of $B_{2\times3}$ to be in Category 1, say
\begin{equation*}
B_{2\times 3 } = \left[\begin{matrix}f_1&f_2&f_3 \\ f_{4}&f_{5}&f_{6}\end{matrix}\right] \gets \left[\begin{matrix}\bm{\mathsf{N}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}} \\ \bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}\end{matrix}\right],
\end{equation*}
and let $W=[e_1,e_4,e_5,e_2,e_3,e_6,e_4,e_1,e_2,e_5,e_6,e_3]$, where $e_i$ is the edge associated to $f_i$. Then $W$ is a TBC walk of length 12 in the protograph. If we take $x=1$, then the composition of the polynomials following Theorem \ref{cycles_and_fixed_points_pp}, in the order prescribed by $W$, gives
\begin{align*}
f_{3}^{-1}&f_{6}f_{5}^{-1}f_{2}f_{1}^{-1}f_{4}f_{6}^{-1}f_{3}f_{2}^{-1}f_{5}f_{4}^{-1}f_{1}(1)= \\
&f_{3+}^{-1}f_{6-}f_{5-}^{-1}f_{2+}f_{1+}^{-1}f_{4-}f_{6-}^{-1}f_{3+}f_{2+}^{-1}f_{5-}f_{4-}^{-1}f_{1+}(1)=1.
\end{align*}
Hence, there is a 12-cycle in the Tanner graph. The analysis for any other combination of three columns in Category 1 is similar and omitted for space constraints. 

Now take all the columns of $B_{2\times3}$ to be in Category 2, say
\begin{equation*}
B_{2\times 3 } = \left[\begin{matrix}f_1&f_2&f_3 \\ f_{4}&f_{5}&f_{6}\end{matrix}\right] \gets \left[\begin{matrix}\bm{\mathsf{N}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}} \\ \bm{\mathsf{N}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}}\end{matrix}\right],
\end{equation*}
and let $W=[e_1,e_4,e_5,e_2,e_3,e_6,e_4,e_1,e_2,e_5,e_6,e_3]$, which is a TBC walk of length 12 in the protograph. If we take $x=1$, then the corresponding composition gives
\begin{align*}
f_{3}^{-1}&f_{6}f_{5}^{-1}f_{2}f_{1}^{-1}f_{4}f_{6}^{-1}f_{3}f_{2}^{-1}f_{5}f_{4}^{-1}f_{1}(1)= \\
&f_{3+}^{-1}f_{6+}f_{5+}^{-1}f_{2+}f_{1+}^{-1}f_{4+}f_{6+}^{-1}f_{3+}f_{2+}^{-1}f_{5+}f_{4+}^{-1}f_{1+}(1)=1.
\end{align*}
Hence, there is a 12-cycle in the Tanner graph. The analysis for any other combination of three columns in Category 2 is similar and omitted for space constraints. 

Now, assume that $B_{2\times3}$ has columns in both Category 1 and Category 2, say
\begin{equation*}
B_{2\times 3 } = \left[\begin{matrix}f_1&f_2&f_3 \\ f_{4}&f_{5}&f_{6}\end{matrix}\right] \gets \left[\begin{matrix}\bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}} \\ \bm{\mathsf{S}}&\bm{\mathsf{N}}&\bm{\mathsf{S}}\end{matrix}\right],
\end{equation*}
and let $W=[e_2,\allowbreak e_5,\allowbreak e_4,\allowbreak e_1,\allowbreak e_2,\allowbreak e_5,\allowbreak e_6,\allowbreak e_3,\allowbreak e_1,\allowbreak e_4,\allowbreak e_5,\allowbreak e_2,\allowbreak e_1,\allowbreak e_4,\allowbreak e_5,\allowbreak e_2,\allowbreak e_3,\allowbreak e_6,\allowbreak e_4,\allowbreak e_1]$, which is a TBC walk of length 20 in the protograph. If we take $x=1$, then the corresponding composition gives
\begin{align*}
	&\begin{aligned}
    f_{1}^{-1}f_{4}f_{6}^{-1}f_{3}f_{2}^{-1}f_{5}&f_{4}^{-1}f_{1}f_{2}^{-1} \cdots \\ &\cdots f_{5}f_{4}^{-1}f_{1}f_{3}^{-1}f_{6}f_{5}^{-1}f_{2}f_{1}^{-1}f_{4}f_{5}^{-1}f_{2}(1)
	\end{aligned} \\
	&\begin{aligned}
	=f_{1+}^{-1}&f_{4+}f_{6+}^{-1}f_{3-}f_{2-}^{-1}f_{5+}f_{4+}^{-1}f_{1+}f_{2+}^{-1}f_{5-}\cdots \\ &\cdots f_{4-}^{-1}f_{1-}f_{3-}^{-1}f_{6+}f_{5+}^{-1}f_{2-}f_{1-}^{-1}f_{4-}f_{5-}^{-1}f_{2+}(1)=1.
	\end{aligned}
\end{align*}
Hence, there is a 20-cycle in the Tanner graph. The analysis for any other combination of two columns in either category and one column in the other category is similar and omitted for space constraints. 

(b) Similar to part (a) and omitted for space constraints.

(c) Three columns from one category are always found.
